user: It is finals week at my college and I'm beyond anxious about it (1)

user: Yes, but they haven't been much help unfortunately.  My classes are online and finals are due when finals are due.  They are not giving any wiggle room (3)

client: While the small victories are comforting, it's been tough with online classes. The rigid schedule for finals is stressful and doesn't leave room for recovery.
therapist: Balancing recovery with a demanding schedule is undoubtedly challenging. Your strategy of celebrating small victories shows resilience. Could planning small moments of rest amidst this stress create a buffer for your wellbeing?

user: No I cannot give up at all.  My scholarship requires me to maintain a certain GPA and I can't afford to lose it (4)
answer_final: It's good to hear that you're not giving up. Sometimes in these situations, you just have to do your best and then at least you know you did what you could. I like to tell myself in these situations that if there are no other avenues to explore, you just have to 'go with the flow' and don't beat yourself up thinking about it over and over - if there's nothing you can do, just do your best to ride it out
client: I understand the importance of resting, but it's hard when my scholarship hinges on maintaining a high GPA. Losing it would be disastrous for my future plans.
therapist: Balancing rest with maintaining your GPA reflects a strong commitment to your goals. How might taking care of yourself enhance your performance and focus, potentially supporting your scholarship?

user: I know, there is just so much riding on these finals.  I have great grades so I'm praying that I pass without any issues and that I don't bomb even one of them (5). Are you still there?
answer_final: If you tried hard previously then you may come out the other end having done very well!  When I was at school a long time ago, I had to stay off school for a month, when they were practising the exams. I didn't get chance to do those and I thought 'wow I'm totally screwed here', but guess what? I did okay!
client: I really hope balancing my health and academics will keep me on track. With finals coming, the pressure is intense. I'm trying hard to pass without risking my scholarship.
therapist: You're showing great strength in managing both your health and academics under pressure. How could acknowledging this perseverance inspire a renewed sense of capability in facing finals while safeguarding your scholarship?

user: I hope that's what happens, I just don't know how to calm down about it (6)
client: Acknowledging my perseverance does help somewhat, yet calming down feels elusive. The looming finals just ramp up anxiety about losing the scholarship.
therapist: Your perseverance truly reflects your inner strength during these stressful times. It's understandable to feel overwhelmed. How might creating small moments of calm amidst the chaos support both your academic and personal wellbeing?

user: Do you know any techniques to help me calm down? (7)
answer_final: It's totally understandable. I think even without the COVID situation, you would still be anxious. It's totally natural. Not that that discounts how you feel. Do you agree?
client: Your suggestion makes me realize I need to incorporate more calming activities. Are there specific techniques or routines you'd recommend to help ease my anxiety during finals?
therapist: Engaging in calming activities can definitely support your focus. Consider incorporating short breathing exercises or mindfulness moments into your routine. These techniques may offer relief and foster balance, helping you face finals with a steadier mind.

user: Yes, that is true.  I just can't quite seem to quiet my mind. (8)
answer_final: Well, I've tried meditating a few times before which doesn;t take it all away, it just takes the edge off! I used a guided meditation app. I also listened to white noise when I went to sleep as I was having trouble sleeping. I find even if you're mind is just taken away from it all for a few minute, it can re-balance you a little
client: I appreciate those suggestions. Breathing exercises might help settle the constant mental chatter and provide clarity during finals. Could you share more about mindfulness techniques?
therapist: Exploring mindfulness can truly offer some peace amidst the chaos. Techniques like focusing on the sensations of each breath or observing thoughts without judgment might provide a quiet space for clarity and grounding. How does incorporating these elements into your finals routine feel to you?

user: I've tried watching some comedy shows and listening to music to take my mind off of it.  It works sometimes (9)
answer_final: Maybe you should do more of that, it sounds like a good idea? Don't feel guilty for doing so either as it acts as a 'medicine'. If the 'medicine' works then take it
